geometry.locator: OSM way/54794245, extract timestamp 2026-09-18; site:soudan-minos-far-detector coordinates (src:minos-prd-2007-muon-charge-ratio); src:fermilab-numi-beam-paper-2016 sec 3 'To point towards the Soudan Laboratory the proton beam had to be inclined downward'
geometry.note: accuracy_m 30 m is dominated by the unsourced assumption that the MINOS Surface Bldg sits directly above the near-detector hall/shaft, not by the OSM footprint (~8 m) or the azimuth (negligible error over a 735 km baseline). Independent cross-check: deriving the target the same way from the OSM NOvA building + the sourced ~1 km NOvA baseline + the bearing to Ash River gives a point 38.6 m away from this one -- good agreement given both chains have their own ~15-30 m uncertainty budgets, and reported here rather than as a formal checks[] row (no independent SOURCED expected value exists for 'distance between the two derivations').

method: Great-circle bearing (336.17 degrees) computed from the OSM 'MINOS Surface Bldg' footprint centroid (way 54794245) to the Soudan far site's own sourced coordinates (47.82027 N, 92.24141 W; cited below), per the NuMI beam paper's statement that the beam points at Soudan. Target placed 1040 m upstream (bearing+180) of that centroid, the sourced MINOS near-detector baseline (src:minos-prl-2016-sterile-search, '1.04 ... km'). Cross-checked (see note) against an independent derivation using the OSM NOvA surface building and the Ash River far site. Note: the far site's own precision (100 m) affects only the bearing here, not a position directly used by this derivation -- at a 735 km baseline a 100 m lateral offset changes the bearing by under 0.01 degrees, negligible next to the 30 m accuracy_m set below (dominated by the unsourced shaft/hall-offset assumption, not by the far-site bearing).
name: NuMI target (derived)
